SMTO-BOOT-0032 — The vLLM installer's helper was started the wrong way

GUID: 62ab29cc-4a56-41f7-b1f9-6dacfdf1f9e4
Slug: boot-vllm-probe-usage
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • vllm_install_support.py is a helper the vLLM installer runs for you. It was started with something other than its two commands, probe or plan, so it did nothing.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. From the SMTO folder, run the installer with your environment name instead of the helper, for example ./src/vllm/install-vllm.sh vllm The installer calls the helper with the right command at the right time.
  2. If you need to run the helper by hand, give it exactly one word, probe or plan, for example python src/vllm/vllm_install_support.py probe The helper accepts only these two commands, with nothing before or after them.
  3. If this appeared while running install-vllm.sh, make sure install-vllm.sh and vllm_install_support.py come from the same SMTO copy. A helper from a different version may not understand the commands the installer sends.

What success looks like

  • The helper prints "CPU:" and "GPU 0:" lines describing your hardware, or the installer continues past this step.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal output, including the SMTO-BOOT-0032 line, plus the exact command you ran, and send it to the person who maintains your SMTO copy. Don't edit the helper to accept other commands.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • vllm_install_support.py exited because its arguments were not exactly probe or exactly plan; it did not probe hardware or fetch release data.

What this means

  • The support script's argv is not exactly probe or exactly plan. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • The support script's argv is not exactly probe or exactly plan.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the full helper argument list and remove unsupported extra arguments.

How to fix it

  • Invoke the helper as python -I src/vllm/vllm_install_support.py probe or with plan (plan runs inside the target environment and needs the packaging module), or let install-vllm.sh call it. If install-vllm.sh triggered this, restore matching copies of install-vllm.sh and vllm_install_support.py from the same checkout.
  • Invoke vllm_install_support.py with probe or plan.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended probe or plan invocation uses the supported syntax.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
